desc: Banff Upper Hot Springs are natural mineral hot springs located in Banff National Park, Alberta, Canada. The springs emerge at 47°C and are rich in minerals including sulfate, calcium, and bicarbonate. They have been a popular bathing destination since the 1880s when the Canadian Pacific Railway brought visitors to the area. The springs are located on Sulphur Mountain at an elevation of 1,585 meters. The historic bathhouse, built in 1935, is a designated heritage building. The springs are one of the most visited natural attractions in the Canadian Rockies, offering mountain views while soaking in the mineral-rich waters.
fact: Banff Upper Hot Springs emerge at 47°C on Sulphur Mountain in the Canadian Rockies · They have been a popular bathing destination since the 1880s · The springs are rich in sulfate, calcium, and bicarbonate minerals · The historic 1935 bathhouse is a designated heritage building

desc: Jigokudani Hot Springs, meaning 'Hell Valley,' is a natural hot spring in Yamanouchi, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. The springs are world-famous for the wild Japanese macaques (snow monkeys) that bathe in the warm waters during winter. The area was originally formed by volcanic activity and features several hot spring pools. The springs emerge at temperatures of 40-50°C. The monkey park was established in 1964 and the snow monkeys have become one of Japan's most iconic wildlife attractions. The springs are located at an elevation of 850 meters in a narrow valley surrounded by steep cliffs and steaming vents.
fact: Jigokudani is famous for wild snow monkeys (Japanese macaques) bathing in the hot springs · The springs emerged from volcanic activity in Nagano, Japan · Hot water emerges at 40-50°C in a narrow valley at 850 meters elevation · The snow monkey park was established in 1964

desc: The Blue Lagoon is a geothermal spa located in a lava field on the Reykjanes Peninsula in southwestern Iceland. It is not a natural hot spring but a man-made lagoon created from the effluent water of the nearby Svartsengi geothermal power plant. The water temperature averages 38-40°C and is rich in silica, algae, and minerals known for their skin-healing properties. The bright blue color comes from the unique silica content that reflects light. The Blue Lagoon is one of Iceland's most visited tourist attractions, attracting over 1.5 million visitors annually. The spa features in-water massage, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar.
fact: The Blue Lagoon is a geothermal spa created from power plant effluent water in Iceland · The bright blue water is rich in silica, algae, and minerals for skin treatment · Water temperature averages 38-40°C in a lava field setting · It attracts over 1.5 million visitors annually

desc: Beppu is Japan's most famous hot spring resort city, located in Oita Prefecture on Kyushu Island. The area has over 2,800 hot spring sources, producing more hot water than any other thermal area in Japan, with a total daily output of about 137,000 kiloliters. The springs are divided into eight distinct geothermal areas known as the 'Beppu Hatto' or Eight Hells of Beppu. Each 'hell' features different types of hot spring activity including boiling mud pools, steam vents, and vividly colored water. Beppu's hot springs, discovered over 1,000 years ago, have been used for therapeutic bathing, cooking, and even power generation.
fact: Beppu has over 2,800 hot spring sources, the most in Japan · Daily hot water output is 137,000 kiloliters · The 'Eight Hells of Beppu' feature boiling mud, steam vents, and colored water · The springs have been used for over 1,000 years for bathing and therapeutic purposes

desc: The Thermal Springs of Saturnia are natural hot springs located in the Maremma region of Tuscany, Italy. The springs emerge at 37.5°C with a flow of about 800 liters per second, the highest flow rate in Europe. The waters are rich in sulfur, carbon dioxide, and beneficial minerals. The Cascate del Mulino are free, natural travertine pools formed by millennia of mineral deposition. The thermal properties have been known since Etruscan and Roman times, with the Romans naming the site after the god Saturn. The water is believed to have therapeutic benefits for skin, respiratory, and circulatory conditions. The springs are situated on the grounds of a historic thermal spa hotel.
fact: Saturnia Springs have the highest hot spring flow rate in Europe at 800 liters/second · The water emerges at 37.5°C, rich in sulfur and beneficial minerals · The Cascate del Mulino are free-access natural travertine pools · The thermal waters have been used since Etruscan and Roman times, named after the god Saturn
